After a tribute video showcased iconic Goldblum performances across his career, including roles in “Invasion of the Body Snatchers,” “The Fly,” “Jurassic Park” and “Independence Day,” the curtain rose to reveal the actor — an accomplished pianist and jazz musician — seated behind a grand piano, from which he performed a medley of songs before a rapt crowd.

Accepting the award after a lengthy standing ovation, Goldblum thanked the Marrakech Film Festival and “the people of Morocco, whose warmth is legendary,” before reflecting on the long journey that brought him to the stage in the Palais des Congrés.

“When I consider the grand artists who have stood on this stage prior to me, I am infinitely humbled,” he said. “This award urges one to look back, and when I do, I don’t see a list of accomplishments. Certainly, I see faces, the people who gave me a chance before I even had earned one. I obviously didn’t get here by myself.”.

He went on to thank the many screenwriters, directors and actors who demonstrated faith in him through the years before insisting that the work they do remains as vital as ever.

“I believe that the stories that we tell matter,” the actor mentioned. “At their best, films let us sit in the dark beside strangers and see the world through somebody else’s eyes. They remind us that we lucky creatures have an unfathomable measure of commonality, and they put to shame all those petty things which seem to divide us.

“Movies also help us imagine something better — a world that works for everyone,” he continued. “That’s a planet toward which I want to keep working for as long as I have breath in my body, and with every story that I might still have the privilege to tell.”.

As well as Saturday’s honors, the Marrakech Film Festival is screening four films from the actor’s decades-spanning career: Lawrence Kasdan’s ’80s ensemble comedy-drama “The Significant Chill,” David Cronenberg’s classic body horror “The Fly,” Roland Emmerich’s alien-invasion blockbuster “Independence Day” and Steven Spielberg’s “Jurassic Park,” the first installment in the dinosaur franchise juggernaut.

The Marrakech Film Festival kicked off Friday night with a star-studded gala screening of Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut,” starring Oscar frontrunner Julianne Moore. Goldblum, who hammed it up on the red carpet outside the Palais alongside wife Emilie Goldblum, spent several minutes working the crowd, at one point stopping to autograph a hand-drawn portrait of the actor that was presented to him by a boisterous fan.

Among the other celebrities in attendance were Swinton and Oscar winner and jury president Marion Cotillard, who heads a jury that includes “Sex Education” star Emma Mackey, “Phantom Thread” actress Vicky Krieps, “All of Us Strangers” filmmaker Andrew Haigh and “The Voice of Hind Rajab” director Kaouther Ben Hania.

Also being honored with a tribute award this week are Moroccan actor Younès Mégri and American screen star John Turturro, whose most recent film, “The Only Living Pickpocket in Latest York,” will screen at the festival. He and Goldblum will both take part in the festival’s Conversation series, along with “Knives Out” director Rian Johnson, “Call Me by Your Name” Oscar nominee Luca Guadagnino, “Fjord” Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, Italian screen icon Monica Bellucci and more.

It has been revealed that the Marrakech Film Festival runs Nov. 20-28.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A creator's video can put a restaurant on someone's weekend list, send shoppers looking for a product, or make a brand want to work with the person who posted it.
  • 18, Snap declared three updates that make it easier for 1) followers to find places their favorite creators recommend, 2) brands to find creators to work with, and 3) agencies to run those campaigns.
  • Here's how each update works and how Snapchat's approach compares with what other social platforms are already doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A creator's video can put a restaurant on someone's weekend list, send shoppers looking for a product, or make a brand want to work with the person who posted it. Snapchat wants to integrate more of that routine into Snapchat.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 18, Snap declared three updates that make it easier for 1) followers to find places their favorite creators recommend, 2) brands to find creators to work with, and 3) agencies to run those campaigns. If you're a creator, that could mean more ways to make money from the videos you already post and another place for people to find your recommendations.

Here's how each update works and how Snapchat's approach compares with what other social platforms are already doing.

Industry observers note that snap Map already works a little like a neighborhood guide. For example, if you tap on a bakery, there's a listing with its hours, directions, and reviews. Now, with a feature called Visited By, Snapchat can also show that a creator you follow has been there and give you a link to their post.

Here's how it works. Using the same bakery example — if a food creator reviews a bakery and tags it in a public post on Spotlight, Snapchat's short-video feed, or posts the review directly to Snap Map with the same tag. Snapchat can then highlight the store on the map for that creator's followers. So if you missed the video when it first went up, you could still come across it while looking for pastry, watch a creator's review, and send the spot to a friend in Chat. The feature is available globally, and Snap notes more than 450 million people use Snap Map each month.

Snap indicates people already share creators' recommendations in Chat when they're talking about "where to go next or what to buy." Visited By gives them a upcoming way to share a business. Snap also sees the sharing part as a way for creators to reach people who don't already follow them.

"For creators, it means more visibility for the places and experiences they share, helping them connect with their existing followers and build new ones as their recommendations are shared with friends," the firm wrote.

This announcement comes a few weeks after TikTok gave its own users an in-app way to go from watching a restaurant video to booking a table. In October, it launched Must Eat, a dining guide built from videos, reviews, and comments across the app.

Snapchat is also changing how advertisers find creators to work with. The revamped Snap Creator Network, now in open beta, lets a brand describe the audience it wants to reach, the type of content it needs, or what it hopes the campaign will accomplish. Snap uses AI to suggest creators, and brands can then review how their content performs, save a shortlist, message creators about a partnership, or pay to promote a post they've already made.

Sources indicate that "Our aim is to make creator discovery and outreach more efficient, while maintaining the creator's voice within their own communities," Snap wrote in the blog post. "For creators, this means greater opportunities to work with some of their favorite brands and be discovered for the right audience fit, not just follower count.".

Eligible creators can opt in by turning on Brand Partnerships in their Public Profile settings. That lets approved brands reach out directly on Snapchat to work together or to use a video the creator has already posted in an ad.

Industry observers note that sometimes the team reaching out to a creator is an agency working on the brand's behalf. Snap is giving those teams more help, too, through its expanded Creator Agency Partner Program. The program, according to Snap, equips "agencies with the training, support, and incentive access they need to build and scale Creator Ads on Snapchat.".

It has been revealed that other social platforms have similar pipelines in place: TikTok One matches advertisers with creators based on a campaign brief, lets brands promote approved posts as Spark Ads, and gives agencies tools to manage contracts and track campaigns. Meta's Creator Marketing Hub, on the other hand, brings creator search, outreach, and Partnership Ads together across Instagram and Facebook.

There's a reason Snap, TikTok, and Meta are all making it easier for brands to find creators and turn their posts into ads. The Interactive Advertising Bureau projected that U.S. creator ad spending would reach $44 billion in 2026, and brands in its research said finding the right creator was their biggest challenge. The easier a platform makes it to find someone, reach out, and run an ad, the better its shot at a slice of that (pretty large) pie.

Stonehenge’s six-ton mystery deepens as scientists narrow their search

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The mystery surrounding Stonehenge's enormous six-ton Altar Stone has taken another turn.
  • A latest study published in the Journal of the Geological Society presents the most comprehensive geological investigation yet of the Altar Stone, offering new clues about one of Stonehenge's most enduring mysteries.
  • Measuring 4.9 meters (about 16 feet) long, the massive sandstone slab lies at the heart of the famous prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in southern England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The mystery surrounding Stonehenge's enormous six-ton Altar Stone has taken another turn. Scientists have eliminated several suspected sources of the ancient sandstone slab, narrowing the search for where it originated thousands of years ago.

A latest study published in the Journal of the Geological Society presents the most comprehensive geological investigation yet of the Altar Stone, offering new clues about one of Stonehenge's most enduring mysteries.

Measuring 4.9 meters (about 16 feet) long, the massive sandstone slab lies at the heart of the famous prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in southern England. For more than a century, archaeologists and geologists believed it had been transported from Wales. However, recent research using advanced analytical methods overturned that long-standing theory and identified northeastern Scotland as a more likely source.

Now, a new international investigation has refined the search even further, although the stone's exact birthplace remains unknown.

New Geological Clues Narrow the Search.

To investigate the Altar Stone's origins, researchers combined fresh observations of the monument with detailed examinations of stone fragments preserved in museum collections.

According to recent reports, using multiple scientific techniques, the team studied the sandstone's physical structure, mineral content, chemical composition, and isotopic signatures. Together, these characteristics provide a distinctive geological fingerprint that can be compared with rock formations across Britain.

The scientists focused particular attention on the Orcadian Basin in northeastern Scotland, an area previously identified as a promising candidate. However, none of the locations examined so far has produced rock with the same combination of characteristics as the Altar Stone.

Although the findings have not revealed the stone's original location, they allow researchers to eliminate several possibilities and concentrate future investigations on more promising areas.

Professor Duncan Pirrie, Emeritus Professor at the University of South Wales and leader of the study, explained:.

Sources indicate that "This is the most comprehensive geological investigation of the Altar Stone ever undertaken. By combining a wide range of analytical techniques, we have built the clearest picture yet of the stone's composition and tested the leading theories about its origins. So far, none of the locations examined have the same set of characteristics as the Altar Stone. That tells us the search is not over, but we are now far better equipped to focus on the areas most likely to yield an answer.".

From Wales to Scotland: A Century-Old Theory Overturned.

For generations, the prevailing explanation placed the Altar Stone's origins in western Wales. That assumption changed when earlier scientific investigations revealed evidence pointing much farther north, toward Scotland.

The latest findings build on that discovery by establishing more precise geological criteria for identifying a potential match.

Professor Richard Bevins, Honorary Professor in the Department of Geography and Earth Sciences at Aberystwyth University, mentioned:.

In a recent development, "For almost a century, the prevailing view was that the Altar Stone came from west Wales. Our previous research overturned that assumption and pointed instead to Scotland as the most likely source. This latest study significantly refines the search by identifying the specific geological characteristics we need to look for, allowing future investigations to be targeted more effectively. With each upcoming piece of evidence, we move closer to solving one of Stonehenge's most enduring mysteries.".

Rather than disproving Scotland as a possible source, the newly introduced investigation helps scientists distinguish between rock formations that appear promising and those that do not match the stone's distinctive properties.

Solving Stonehenge's Six-Ton Mystery.

In a recent development, determining where the Altar Stone came from could reveal much more than the birthplace of a single rock. It could also help explain how prehistoric communities acquired and transported enormous stones over remarkable distances.

Stonehenge was constructed in multiple stages between approximately 3000 and 1600 BC. Its builders are known to have moved massive stones across the landscape, including the smaller bluestones, which traveled roughly 225 kilometers (140 miles) from western Wales.

Industry observers note that if the Altar Stone originated in northeastern Scotland, its journey to Salisbury Plain would have been considerably longer. Establishing its precise source could therefore offer important clues about the transportation methods, organization, and engineering abilities of the people who built Stonehenge.

Professor Nick Pearce, Emeritus Professor of Geochemistry in the Department of Geography and Earth Sciences at Aberystwyth University, emphasized why eliminating possible sources represents genuine progress:.

It has been revealed that "In a geological detective story such as this, ruling out potential source areas is just as important as identifying new ones. Every location eliminated narrows the search and brings us closer to discovering where the Altar Stone originated. The stone is unique among those at Stonehenge, and tracing its source would provide valuable new insights into its remarkable journey to Salisbury Plain thousands of years ago.".

It has been revealed that the researchers believe the detailed geological fingerprint developed during this investigation will guide future searches and could eventually identify the Altar Stone's original location. Such a discovery would help illuminate one of prehistoric Britain's most extraordinary engineering accomplishments.

The international research team included geologists and archaeologists from the United Kingdom, Canada, Italy, and Sweden. Participating organizations included the University of South Wales, Aberystwyth University, University College London, the University of Aberdeen, the University of Plymouth, the James Hutton Institute, the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, the University of Milano-Bicocca, and several industry partners.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station debuted into orbit.
  • Industry observers note that the 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus.
  • In a recent development, zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station debuted into orbit.

Industry observers note that the 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya debuted on board a Russian Proton rocket. Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit.

In a recent development, zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

Sources indicate that today, the International Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze.

It has been revealed that as of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece.

And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station.

Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet.

In a recent development, NASA paid $220 million for Zarya's construction at the Krunichev State Research and Production Space Center in Moscow, with work beginning in 1994 and ending in 1998. The module is a central hub based on the success of Russia's Salyut space station designs, with two solar arrays for power and 16 external tanks to store propellant.

While NASA's space shuttle Endeavour was the first to meet Zarya (and attach NASA's core Unity connecting module to it), it wasn't until Russia'z Zvezda service debuted in 2000 and docked with Zarya's aft that the fledgling space station was large enough to accomodate its first three-person crew, Expedition 1.

Over the last 28 years, giant backbone-like metal trusses, solar wings and many other modules (built by Russia, NASA, Europe, Canada and Japan) have greatly expanded the living area of the station. Many ISS components could not be tested with one another on the ground, meaning the first time they were attached was in space during construction.

The result is a feat of space construction that has only recently seen a rival as China works to expand its own Tiangong space station.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures.
  • In a recent development, the discovery occurred during an expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard.
  • Recent findings suggest that members of MBARI's Biodiversity and Biooptics Team were investigating marine life approximately 90 kilometers (55 miles) offshore when they spotted the fish about 600 meters (1,970 feet) below the surface.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures. Researchers from the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) spotted a barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma), a mysterious species known for its transparent head and remarkable eyes that can rotate to track prey.

In a recent development, the discovery occurred during an expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard. It marked only the eleventh time MBARI scientists have encountered this elusive fish during nearly four decades of ocean exploration.

Recent findings suggest that members of MBARI's Biodiversity and Biooptics Team were investigating marine life approximately 90 kilometers (55 miles) offshore when they spotted the fish about 600 meters (1,970 feet) below the surface. Using the remotely operated vehicle (ROV) Doc Ricketts, the researchers were filming and collecting deep-sea organisms when the unexpected visitor appeared.

"Seeing a barreleye fish is a rare treat. Crew from across the ship joined the science team in the control room, mesmerized by this remarkable animal. Deep-sea animals capture the imagination, creating wonder and awe that we hope will inspire stewardship of the largest living space on Earth," remarked Senior Scientist Steven Haddock.

[See video link after end of article.].

A Surprise Encounter Deep in the Pacific Ocean.

It has been revealed that the discovery was an unexpected highlight of the eight-day Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters expedition. Haddock and his colleagues had primarily been investigating gelatinous marine animals, including jellyfish, siphonophores, and ctenophores, also known as comb jellies. Their research seeks to understand how these delicate organisms have evolved to survive in the open ocean at great depths.

In a recent development, to investigate life throughout the water column, the team combined blue-water scuba dives near the surface with remotely operated vehicle surveys hundreds of meters below. These complementary approaches allowed researchers to observe and collect animals living in very different parts of the ocean.

The barreleye appeared just as the day's underwater operations were coming to an end. The ROV pilots were "flying" Doc Ricketts toward the surface for recovery when Research Specialist Shannon Johnson noticed the unusual fish and immediately asked them to stop.

Sources indicate that most of the scientists had already moved to the ship's wet lab, where they were preparing to catalog specimens collected during the dive. When word spread about the sighting, they hurried back to the control room, accompanied by crew members eager to see the extraordinary animal. The rare encounter provided an exciting conclusion to a busy and productive week of exploration.

How the Barreleye Fish Uses Its Transparent Head to Hunt.

It has been revealed that the barreleye's strange appearance is more than a biological curiosity. Its unusual anatomy helps it find food in the ocean's twilight zone, a dimly lit region where sunlight is faint and spotting prey can be difficult.

Earlier observations by MBARI Senior Scientist Bruce Robison and Research Specialist Kim Reisenbichler helped scientists understand how this remarkable fish hunts.

Industry observers note that rather than constantly swimming in search of food, Macropinna can remain nearly motionless in the water, supported by its large fins, which provide both stability and precise control over its movements. Its tubular eyes normally point upward, allowing it to watch for the faint silhouettes of animals passing overhead.

Once the fish detects something worth eating, its eyes can rotate within a transparent dome of tissue covering the top of its head. This unusual ability allows the barreleye to maintain visual contact with prey as it changes position to capture it.

According to recent reports, the clear, gelatinous covering serves another vital purpose. Barreleyes can feed on small crustaceans trapped among the stinging tentacles of deep-sea siphonophores, which are colonial animals related to jellyfish. The protective dome helps shield the fish's sensitive eyes while it retrieves its meal.

Rare 4K Footage Reveals Extraordinary Details.

It has been revealed that scientists were able to spend approximately 20 minutes watching the barreleye during the encounter. Using the high-resolution 4K camera aboard Doc Ricketts, they recorded unusually detailed views of its anatomy and movements.

According to recent reports, the team also adjusted the vehicle's lighting to make the fish's transparent head shield easier to observe. These changes helped reveal the unusual structures that make this species so distinctive.

ROV Pilot/Technician Cameron Law brought Doc Ricketts close enough to capture additional footage with the vehicle's virtual reality camera. The resulting 3D stereo imagery provides another perspective on the fish and could eventually be used in educational programs and public outreach.

It has been revealed that "Macropinna reminds us of the surprising ways that animals have adapted to thrive in the ocean's midwater," noted Haddock. "So many of them survive by looking for subtle optical cues, like a shadow passing overhead, and this sets off evolutionary competition, pitting bioluminescent camouflage against increasingly sophisticated visual capabilities.".

An Extraordinary Sighting After Nearly 7,000 Deep-Sea Dives.

Industry observers note that the rarity of the encounter becomes even more striking when considering MBARI's extensive exploration history. Over nearly 40 years, the institute has conducted approximately 7,000 remotely operated vehicle dives and accumulated more than 41,000 hours of deep-sea video. Despite that enormous effort, researchers have recorded just 11 encounters with Macropinna microstoma.

MBARI's previous sighting of Macropinna occurred in 2021. The latest encounter represents two important firsts for the institute: its first 4K footage of this species and its first observation of the fish from the new flagship research vessel David Packard.

According to recent reports, MBARI scientists have also encountered other members of the barreleye family during their ocean expeditions. This summer, researchers working with Schmidt Ocean Institute in the mid-Atlantic Ocean recorded another unusual deep-sea species, the binocular fish (Winteria telescopa).

Together, these encounters provide rare opportunities to observe the remarkable adaptations that allow animals to survive far beneath the ocean's surface, where light is scarce and much of the marine environment remains unexplored.

The Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters expedition was supported through the David and Lucile Packard Foundation's longstanding commitment to MBARI's scientific research.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, rockstar Games went above and beyond licensing dozens of existing bangers across almost any genre you can imagine for GTA 6's in-game radio stations, and that's before you even get to the fantastic original score from Justice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most important aspects of any Grand Theft Auto game is the soundtrack, and for the first time in the series, GTA 6 doesn't require players to be in a car or near a radio to listen to it.

According to recent reports, rockstar Games went above and beyond licensing dozens of existing bangers across almost any genre you can imagine for GTA 6's in-game radio stations, and that's before you even get to the fantastic original score from Justice. However, one small limitation of previous games in the series was that you couldn't really enjoy all of that music while walking around.

Thankfully, Rockstar Games took a cue from how people listen to music in 2026. Here is how to listen to music in GTA 6 without driving a car.

In a recent development, in real life, most people have a pair of headphones or earbuds handy so they can listen to music on their phones. GTA 6 joins some other open-world action games like Watch Dogs 2 in allowing players to use virtual headphones to jam out to some tunes from a smart device while simply walking around the world. The best part is that you can do this from a very early point in the game, though it will require a little bit of in-game money.

Sources indicate that protagonist Jason Duval is perhaps the only guy in Leonida who doesn't own headphones of any kind at the start of GTA 6, so you'll have to go buy some. This can be done at any electronics store in Vice City and the surrounding areas, and you'll know a store sells headphones if the store's icon on the in-game map is a pair of headphones. Convenient!

Unless you really branch out right away and decide to explore the whole map before getting on with the story, the easiest way to get headphones at the start is to drive up north from Jason's neighborhood to the town of Hamlet. Some of the early main story missions will take you there, anyway. What you're looking for is a store called Zeke's Electronics on the north side of Hamlet.

Simply go in and you'll be able to buy either over-ear headphones or earbuds next to the cash register. Over-ear cans will run you about $200, while earbuds cost $119. I can't tell if there's a meaningful difference between the two aside from looks, so just go with whatever you like more.

It has been revealed that once you have your headphones, simply hold left on the D-pad to listen to the radio while outside of a car. I recommend the Dirty South Classics station, personally, but your mileage may vary. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m.
  • The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX released a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.

It has been revealed that A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317.

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.

SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit.

Recent findings suggest that USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world.

NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions.

USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November.

The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites.

Industry observers note that the Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025, for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out. SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights.

In a recent development, michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. #47653. Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1148 w)

Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1148 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Exercising too intensely without enough recovery time may affect more than muscles and physical endurance.
  • In a new study published in the journal Neuroscience, researchers in Brazil found that prolonged, exhausting exercise altered dopamine regulation in the hippocampus, a brain region crucial for memory and emotional regulation.
  • The scientists observed that mice exposed to demanding exercise schedules continued to have elevated dopamine levels during periods when they should have been recovering.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Exercising too intensely without enough recovery time may affect more than muscles and physical endurance. New research suggests that excessive training can also disrupt brain chemistry, potentially interfering with the processes that help the brain return to its normal resting state.

In a new study published in the journal Neuroscience, researchers in Brazil found that prolonged, exhausting exercise altered dopamine regulation in the hippocampus, a brain region crucial for memory and emotional regulation.

The scientists observed that mice exposed to demanding exercise schedules continued to have elevated dopamine levels during periods when they should have been recovering. Dopamine plays an key role in motivation and alertness, and the researchers believe that similar disruptions in humans could help explain why excessive training is sometimes associated with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue. If confirmed, this connection would provide further evidence that sufficient rest is essential for both physical fitness and mental well-being.

"Our findings show that excessive physical exercise affects not only skeletal muscle but also has a pronounced impact on the brain," said Alisson Luiz da Rocha, the study's first author.

Rocha carried out the research during his doctoral studies at the Ribeirão Preto School of Physical Education and Sports at the University of São Paulo (EEFERP-USP) in Brazil, supported by a scholarship from FAPESP. He explained that the findings demonstrate how exercise influences the central nervous system, with effects extending well beyond muscle development.

How Scientists Simulated Overtraining.

To investigate what happens in the brain when exercise becomes excessive, the team studied two main groups of mice exposed to different levels of physical activity.

Industry observers note that one group completed a single strenuous treadmill session, running until they reached exhaustion. The other followed an extended training program designed to reproduce the demanding conditions associated with overtraining syndrome in elite athletes.

Overtraining syndrome occurs when the physical demands of training exceed the body's ability to recover. It can cause declining athletic performance, reduced appetite, ongoing fatigue, muscle pain, and a greater risk of injuries. Changes in immune function and metabolism are also common.

For the extended training experiment, the mice exercised over eight weeks as the researchers gradually increased the workload. By the final week, they were completing two sessions each day, with only four hours of recovery between workouts.

According to recent reports, after the exercise programs, the scientists examined the animals' hippocampi. They measured dopamine and serotonin, along with proteins involved in producing and managing these chemical messengers. These included tyrosine hydroxylase (TyrH), an enzyme needed for dopamine production, and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2), which helps package neurotransmitters for release.

Dopamine Remained Elevated for 48 Hours.

According to recent reports, in mice that completed just one exhausting treadmill session, dopamine levels increased shortly after exercise. This showed that even a single bout of intense activity could produce a measurable chemical response in the brain.

Sources indicate that the more striking results came from the animals that underwent weeks of demanding training. In this group, both dopamine and TyrH remained elevated for 48 hours after the performance test, even though the mice were in their recovery period.

According to recent reports, this prolonged response suggests that repeated strenuous exercise without sufficient rest may interfere with the brain's normal regulation of dopamine. Rather than promptly returning to its usual chemical state, the brain continued to show signs of altered neurotransmitter activity long after the exercise had ended.

Adelino Sanchez Ramos da Silva, a professor at EEFERP-USP who coordinated the study, explained that finding comparable changes in humans could help researchers better understand the possible connections between overtraining, brain chemistry, and sleep disturbances.

Industry observers note that however, the researchers caution that the study did not directly measure sleep, anxiety, or alertness. Those possible consequences remain to be investigated, and additional research is needed to determine whether the same dopamine changes occur in people.

Dopamine is often associated with pleasure and motivation, but it also helps regulate wakefulness and other essential brain functions. Its presence is not harmful on its own. What matters is whether its activity remains appropriately balanced.

According to Rocha, difficulties could arise if dopamine remains unusually elevated when the brain should be preparing for sleep. Such changes could also disrupt the balance between dopamine and other neurotransmitters, potentially affecting how the nervous system regulates activity and rest.

It has been revealed that another notable finding involved serotonin, a neurotransmitter that has long been investigated for its possible role in fatigue. Despite the substantial changes in dopamine, the researchers detected no significant differences in serotonin levels between the animals.

Industry observers note that this result challenges the long-standing idea that serotonin alone is primarily responsible for excessive fatigue. Instead, the findings suggest that changes in dopamine regulation may also deserve attention when scientists investigate the biological effects of overtraining.

Why Recovery Is Essential for the Brain and Body.

Although the connection between these chemical changes and symptoms such as insomnia or anxiety has not yet been established in humans, the findings reinforce the importance of allowing sufficient time for recovery.

Excessive training without adequate rest can undermine the benefits of exercise, contributing to reduced performance, persistent muscle pain, and problems with immune function. The latest results suggest that changes in brain chemistry may be another vital part of this process.

Industry observers note that for recreational exercisers and professional athletes alike, the researchers emphasize that training should be balanced with appropriate recovery and expert guidance. Increasing workout intensity does not necessarily produce better results if the body is not given enough time to adapt.

Industry observers note that rocha also conducted research during a postdoctoral fellowship at the School of Applied Sciences (FCA) of the State University of Campinas (UNICAMP) in Limeira. This work included an internship at the University of Michigan in the United States, where he right now works as a researcher.

Additional funding came from a Thematic Project led by Silva, a postdoctoral fellowship awarded to Ana Paula Pinto, and a direct doctorate scholarship supporting João Pedro Floriano. Both Pinto and Floriano are affiliated with EEFERP-USP.

According to recent reports, the team is now participating in a latest international research project aimed at identifying which biological systems first begin to show signs of strain when exercise exceeds the level at which it normally produces beneficial adaptations. Understanding these early warning signals could help scientists determine when productive training begins to become harmful.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (927 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most crucial temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.
  • Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.
  • The Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most crucial temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.

Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.

The Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art. The sculptures adorning its pediments, created under the direction of the legendary sculptor Phidias, are considered unparalleled examples of proportion and grace. They have influenced artists from ancient Rome through Neoclassicism to the modern era.

The east pediment above the temple entrance depicted the birth of the goddess Athena from the head of her father Zeus, surrounded by the Olympian gods. A total of 39 figures adorned the roughly 29-meter-long work of art. At its center stood a colossal Zeus figure, measuring 3.8 meters in height.

For centuries, scholars have puzzled over exactly what the arrangement looked like, as the pediment was destroyed during the Christianization of Greece.

But now there has been a breakthrough.

After decades of painstaking detective work and with the help of modern technology, archaeologist Vinzenz Brinkmann and his team have managed to piece together all the surviving fragments of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Industry observers note that brinkmann heads the Antiquities and Asia department at Frankfurt's Liebieghaus sculpture collection. "We're very, very confident that we've solved the mystery," he told DW.

The results are now on display in an exhibition at the Liebieghaus titled "Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle.".

Industry observers note that only around 20% of the original marble sculpture's volume is known to have survived. The fragments are scattered across various European museums, with most located in Athens. The British Museum also holds numerous pieces.

Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, have spent more than 40 years working on this ancient puzzle, with so many of its pieces missing.

And they were far from the first to attempt it: "Already in the 19th century, many scholars studied the subject and developed well-founded theories based on their deep knowledge of ancient sources," Brinkmann explains.

In 1910, a study documenting the many fragments held by the British Museum was published. The research team was able to build on that earlier work, but progress remained slow for years.

Industry observers note that then, in 2014, a visit to the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg provided Brinkmann with a crucial clue. There, he encountered a Roman sarcophagus featuring a relief of Athena's birth. "That's when it suddenly clicked: They're all there!".

In a recent development, nine such sarcophagi are known to exist, almost all of them in Rome. Each depicts a different section of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Brinkmann emphasizes that other scholars had already noticed this connection in the 19th century. "But we really seized on the idea and never let go.".

Sources indicate that the researchers also benefited from 21st-century technology: 3D scanners and printers. Brinkmann and his team visited numerous destinations to examine around 60 original fragments at different locations — traveling light. An iPhone was all they needed to scan the pieces.

In a recent development, digitally fitting the fragments together led to another important discovery. "We know these figures we're putting together!" Brinkmann recalls thinking at the time.

The Romans had repeatedly made individual copies of all the sculptures from the pediment. "These copies matched the fragments perfectly. Suddenly, we found ourselves surrounded by old acquaintances we had never suspected had come from the pediment." This finally enabled the researchers to reconstruct all the figures and their original arrangement.

Using a 3D printer, the team created a 4-meter-long model at a scale of 1:7.7. For the exhibition, they also produced life-size 3D prints of the most key fragments and mounted them on panels depicting the complete figures at their original size. An animation brings the reconstructed composition to life, digitally assembling the fragments to reveal how the east pediment once looked.

According to recent reports, alongside works from the Liebieghaus collection, the exhibition features loans from other institutions, including the Vatican Museums and the Louvre. Objects from the Acropolis Museum in Athens had originally been expected as well. But Greece withdrew its participation after learning that the British Museum was also planning to lend fragments to the Frankfurt exhibition. The Liebieghaus ultimately decided to forgo the British-owned fragments, too.

According to recent reports, there is a reason for this controversy. Britain holds a substantial portion of the Parthenon frieze as well as fragments from both pediments.

Greek authorities have been campaigning for their return for decades.

In Britain, the 56 sections of the frieze are known as the "Elgin Marbles," named after Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire in Constantinople.

In the early 19th century, Elgin had sculptures removed from the exterior of the Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens. They were taken to Britain with the consent of the Ottoman Empire, which ruled Greece at the time.

Britain maintains that the sculptures were legally acquired.

Greece, however, considers them stolen.

For years, the dispute remained deadlocked. Since the Labour Party came to power in Britain, there has been some movement toward resolving it. But apparently not enough to persuade Greece to lend artworks to an exhibition in which the British Museum might also participate.

Sources indicate that the exhibition "Athena, the Stage is Yours. The Parthenon Puzzle" runs through July 25, 2027, at the Liebieghaus in Frankfurt.

This article was originally written in German.

U.S. officially loses measles elimination status amid ongoing outbreaks

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • on Tuesday lost its official designation as a measles-free nation, more than 25 years after it eliminated the highly contagious virus.
  • The Pan American Health Organization announced the decision, which came after an independent panel of eight scientific experts convened last week to consider the country's epidemiological evidence.
  • In other words, measles is spreading regularly in the country again, with ongoing outbreaks sparking fresh ones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The U.S. on Tuesday lost its official designation as a measles-free nation, more than 25 years after it eliminated the highly contagious virus.

The Pan American Health Organization announced the decision, which came after an independent panel of eight scientific experts convened last week to consider the country's epidemiological evidence. The director of PAHO, the regional branch of the World Health Organization, made the final call that measles is endemic — or always present — in the U.S. following 12 months of continuous transmission.

In other words, measles is spreading regularly in the country again, with ongoing outbreaks sparking fresh ones.

Recent findings suggest that "The commission concluded that endemic measles transmission has now been reestablished in Bolivia, Mexico and the United States, and recommended that their measles elimination status be withdrawn — a recommendation which I have accepted," Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO director, said during a news briefing on Tuesday.

In a recent development, it's a devastating step backward for American public health, as declining childhood vaccination rates and vaccine hesitancy fuel outbreaks across the country that have sickened thousands of people and led to a tragic string of preventable deaths. Among the deaths where vaccination status was reported, all were unvaccinated.

More than 5,400 measles cases had been reported nationwide in 2026 as of mid-November, marking the country's worst outbreak in more than three decades. States have confirmed 10 deaths associated with the disease so far in 2026: seven in Pennsylvania, one in Newly introduced York and two in Wisconsin.

According to recent reports, the commission found that out of 52 U.S. states and territories it tracked, 48 experienced measles outbreaks during the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, PAHO Assistant Director Dr. Rhonda Sealey-Thomas noted during the briefing. But Barbosa said the countries are already taking action to control outbreaks, such as strengthening vaccination, surveillance for timely case detection and outbreak response efforts.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. in particular has ramped up vaccination efforts to close immunity gaps, particularly in areas with low immunization coverage experiencing outbreaks, said Dr. Daniel Salas, executive manager of PAHO's Special Program for Comprehensive Immunization. He said PAHO expects the U.S. to present its corrective action initiative in the coming weeks, outlining strategies to regain its designation.

In a Tuesday release, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention noted it will continue to ensure all communities have the resources to prevent and respond to outbreaks and is committed to working with states and other local partners to restore the U.S.'s measles elimination status.

Sources indicate that CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz remarked in the release that the measles elimination designation "is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does." She said the agency has invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach communities where transmission is occurring.

Sources indicate that last week, Schwartz told Reuters that the agency is going to be "doing the same exact thing that we've been doing today" if the U.S. loses its measles-free status.

It has been revealed that the decision also poses a fresh test for the Trump administration and its Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has taken steps to change recommendations for the childhood measles, mumps and rubella, or MMR, vaccine and has a long history of questioning its safety without evidence.

But Kennedy, in a Tuesday X post, noted he continues to recommend MMR vaccination as "the most effective way to prevent measles.".

"We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," Kennedy said. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment.".

According to recent reports, CNBC previously reported on how the return of measles in the U.S. exposes weaknesses in the nation's public health system that raise concerns about the return of other eliminated diseases. The resurgence of measles exposes eroding trust in health institutions and growing challenges in persuading people to protect themselves, their children and their communities.

Public health experts previously told CNBC that the return of measles ultimately boils down to fewer children getting vaccinated.

The MMR vaccine is about 97% effective against measles after two doses, while a single dose is 93% effective, according to the CDC. Yet data aggregated by the CDC demonstrates that vaccination coverage for that shot among U.S. kindergarteners fell to 92.4% in the 2025-2026 school year, which is below the 95% threshold public health officials generally recommend to prevent sustained transmission.

The American Medical Association urged the public to get vaccinated after PAHO's announcement.

"We must treat the current measles outbreaks as an urgent call to rebuild trust in science-based recommendations and restore strong, fully-funded public health infrastructure to protect families and communities and prevent the return of diseases once eliminated," AMA President Dr. Willie Underwood remarked in a statement.

In a separate statement, the pharmaceutical industry's largest lobbying group called on policymakers to provide "clear, accurate information about the seriousness of measles infection and the effectiveness of vaccines against it, restore and sustain high vaccination coverage in every community, strengthen vaccination efforts, and invest in disease surveillance and rapid outbreak response.".

It has been revealed that "We have the tools to eliminate measles again and what we need now is the commitment to use them," remarked Dr. Michael Ybarra, chief medical officer of the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America.

Measles isn't just a public health threat — it's also a huge financial burden on the healthcare system, CNBC reported.

Recent findings suggest that based on this year's case count, a newly introduced tool developed by researchers at Johns Hopkins University estimates an economic cost of nearly $83 million for the outbreaks. That total includes $56 million in public health response costs, almost $25 million in lost productivity and more than $1.8 million in direct medical expenses.

The U.S. now joins Canada, Spain and the U.K., which all recently lost their measles-free status after a review by experts at the World Health Organization. While the U.S. dropped out of the WHO, it remains a member of PAHO, its Americas branch.

It has been revealed that thankfully, Rockstar Games has kept streamers and content creators in mind and gave them an easy way to shut off licensed music. Here's how to do it.

Simply pause the game by pressing the option or menu button on your controller.

Next, scroll down to the Settings option.

In the Settings menu, head to the very last tab labeled Audio.

Finally, scroll down to Mute Licensed Music and toggle this option on.

This option will mute all the licensed music in the game and ensure your streams and videos don't get taken down.

According to recent reports, there are some things to note. Rockstar Games does not provide any royalty-free replacement music. If a licensed song is playing on the radio in-game, owners won't hear anything until a radio show host or original song comes on. With that said, original music created for the game will continue to play. In addition, captions for licensed music will still appear on screen even though the music won't be audible.

It has been revealed that you can always roll the dice and hope a song played on the radio in GTA 6 doesn't take down your stream or clip. But, this Mute Licensed Music option will help you avoid any potential problems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I've been testing smart bird feeders for more than two years in my own backyard, and Birdfy has been—and still is—the brand I trust and recommend most. These feeders are well-made, reliable, and reasonably priced. The brand's app is also excellent; it's easy to navigate and use without shelling out for an additional subscription. Better still, Birdfy just rolled out free lifetime AI ID (which is quite decent) with any bird feeder, including the lowest-priced models. If you don't want to gift a traditional feeder, you might consider Birdfy's smart birdbath and nesting box, each of which comes equipped with the same high-quality camera(s).

Below are the models I've tested—in some cases for years—and recommend, including a couple I personally plan to buy as gifts this year.

Industry observers note that WIRED first reviewed this feeder in 2022. Back then we loved the concept, but felt its AI ID didn't quite cut it. Birdfy has come a long way since then on the AI front. The feeder body is largely the same, but the app and AI ID (now free) are both much improved, offering a seamless and user-friendly experience that makes it easy to sort through which birds visited that day. This once-pricey feeder is now at the lowest price I have ever seen for the version without the solar panel. The 5200-mAh rechargeable battery lasts a few weeks, but I think it's convenient to not have to bring it in to charge, if you want to spring for the extra $20 for that solar panel.

In a recent development, birdfy's “beginner” model, this unit is basically a gravity pet feeder with a camera on the side. All you need to do is snap three pieces together, charge the camera, and pair it to the Birdfy app. If you know anyone who loves birds but is intimidated by the thought of having to set up and calibrate a smart bird feeder, this could be the perfect gift for them. However, note that my test unit keeps losing its lid on windy days, and there's no roof to keep the seed from getting wet on rainy days, so it's probably best for summer use. I also just discovered that Walmart carries an exclusive periwinkle color that looks lovely.

Industry observers note that birdfy's Metal 2 4K is the brand's flagship release for this year, with Ultra 4K resolution and dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz) Wi-Fi connection. The metal body claims to resist squirrels, and the muted green color is a welcome change from Birdfy's usual bright plastics. As was the case with the brand's previous flagship, the Feeder 2 Pro, I had some significant connection issues with the Metal 2 4K. This kept it from being a top pick in my guide to the Best Smart Bird Feeders, but the model is still worth a mention here due to its combination of features and build quality, as well as Birdfy's excellent customer service if something does go wrong.

Sources indicate that smart bird feeders aren't always the most aesthetically pleasing thing you could put in your yard, but Birdfy's 2K bamboo model was the first smart feeder I've ever had that actually garnered compliments. The natural wood and waterfall-style black roof complement any landscaping or exterior decor, and the camera and overall setup ran flawlessly for me during my months of testing. Just make sure you apply varnish or urethane regularly to the bamboo, as the finish on mine peeled after only two months in mild weather.

This interesting product pairs a plastic birdbath (on an optional metal stand) with a solar-powered camera, so you can keep an eye on visiting birds without having to deal with seed mess. When I first tested it, I was worried birds would splash water on the camera lens, but the most popular activity at the bath is by far drinking the water (birds, raccoons, squirrels … anything passing by). I don't love that the basin grows algae rapidly and the pump clogs easily, but this is otherwise a very well-made item—it's been in my yard for a year and a half through every season, and while the plastic is starting to fade a bit, it's still going strong.

Industry observers note that though I do love a smart bird feeder, Birdfy's Nest Duo is the absolute zenith of bird-watching for me. A black-capped chickadee moved in, laid eggs, and raised chicks (detailed here), and the cameras and app on the Nest stayed working, giving me 24-hour updates with interior night vision and views of the entry hole's exterior to see who was coming and going. A remote control on a 10-foot-long cord lets you reset or charge the camera without bothering the birds (though the auxiliary solar panel worked great for me). Note, however, that the black waterfall-style roof and lack of ventilation do pose a risk of overheating any young birds; during a May heat wave, I had to affix an umbrella and ice packs to the box, but the interior thermometer and hygrometer did a great job keeping me abreast of changing conditions.

European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth.
  • Sources indicate that the BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov.
  • Industry observers note that the big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth.

Sources indicate that the BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.

Industry observers note that the big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes.

BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

The duo introduced — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018, beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system.

Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun. Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug.

So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year, however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters.

Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total.

Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts.

According to recent reports, shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027.

BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world.

"The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind, to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description.

"The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. #47646. This strange creature lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (918 w)

This strange creature lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fossil discovered in Illinois years ago has turned out to belong to a previously unrecognized species that lived 309 million years ago, long before dinosaurs appeared.
  • Recent findings suggest that during the Carboniferous period, the region surrounding present-day Chicago looked dramatically different.
  • In a recent development, the newly identified species, Jeanerpeton mazonensis, resembled a salamander with the short, stocky body of a frog.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fossil discovered in Illinois years ago has turned out to belong to a previously unrecognized species that lived 309 million years ago, long before dinosaurs appeared. The strange animal, an early relative of modern amphibians, has also received a name with a personal connection to the two student scientists who helped identify it.

Recent findings suggest that during the Carboniferous period, the region surrounding present-day Chicago looked dramatically different. Instead of a modern city, the landscape was a warm, swampy river delta populated by giant insects, early animals adapted to life on land, and unusual creatures swimming through its waterways. This environment supported an extraordinary variety of life, leaving behind fossils that now provide a remarkable glimpse into Earth's prehistoric past.

In a recent development, the newly identified species, Jeanerpeton mazonensis, resembled a salamander with the short, stocky body of a frog. Its name means "Jean's crawler from Mazon Creek," honoring the mothers of the two student researchers, both of whom are named Jean. The discovery is described in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

A 309-Million-Year-Old Fossil With Extraordinary Detail.

The Mazon Creek fossil deposits are among the world's most crucial sources of Carboniferous fossils, in large part because of the conditions that existed when the animals were alive.

Recent findings suggest that as plants and animals died in the ancient river delta, layers of sediment quickly covered their remains. This rapid burial created ideal conditions for fossilization, sometimes preserving delicate structures that would ordinarily disappear long before they could become fossils.

"What's really cool about Mazon Creek is that it preserves all of these unusual details -- things like toe pads and body outlines," indicates Allison Sefcovic, co-lead author of the paper and 2025 Women in Science intern at the Field.

Industry observers note that "In the fossil of Jeanerpeton, we can see some of the scales on its back and tiny 'belly ribs' called gastralia. You can even see the eye impressions! It's so cool to see.".

These exceptionally preserved features offer valuable evidence of what early amphibian relatives looked like. They also indicate that several anatomical characteristics associated with modern frogs and salamanders were already present approximately 309 million years ago.

A Prehistoric Species Hidden in Plain Sight.

Although Jeanerpeton mazonensis has only recently been formally described, its fossil was discovered many years earlier. An amateur fossil collector originally found the specimen and later donated it to the Field Museum.

Industry observers note that when researchers first examined it, they classified the animal as Amphibamus grandiceps, a previously established species known from the Mazon Creek area. However, closer examination eventually revealed that the fossil represented a distinct animal.

Misidentifications like this can occur when scientists have limited information about ancient species. Fossils that appear similar are sometimes assigned to an existing species even when vital differences have not yet been recognized.

Paleontologists refer to such broad classifications as a "waste bin taxon." The term describes a category in which multiple fossils are grouped together because they seem related, even though their true identities and evolutionary relationships remain poorly understood.

"What we're finding from the Field Museum's collection are a bunch of things that historically were grouped together into this waste bin taxon known as Amphibamus grandiceps," states Cam So, co-author on the study and postdoctoral researcher at the Field Museum.

Recent findings suggest that "Jeanerpeton is one of those species. And now, we've found enough evidence to support it being an anatomically distinct animal. With this publication, we officially pull Jeanerpeton out of this waste bin taxon.".

The finding highlights how museum collections can continue to produce discoveries long after fossils are first collected. In this case, a specimen already held by the Field Museum provided enough anatomical evidence to establish a separate species.

Two Student Scientists Make a Remarkable Discovery.

The research was co-led by Payton Kohlberg and Allison Sefcovic, who participated in the Field Museum's Women in Science internship program in 2025. The initiative encourages young women to explore careers in scientific research and museums.

Both students worked alongside So as members of the research group led by Arjan Mann, the museum's assistant curator of fossil fishes and early tetrapods in the Negaunee Integrative Research Center.

For Kohlberg, the project offered an opportunity to enter an unfamiliar scientific field and gain confidence through hands-on research.

"Before working in the Mann Lab, I didn't know much about paleontology," claims Kohlberg. "My experience at the Field and in the Women in Science program has made me more confident in my abilities to try something new. It is scary to take on a project when you feel like you don't know as much as you should, but I learned with my practical experience that it is possible to overcome that fear with hard work.".

The identification of Jeanerpeton mazonensis adds another species to the growing record of ancient life preserved at Mazon Creek. As researchers continue examining fossils from the region, each discovery helps reveal more about the extraordinary diversity of animals and plants that inhabited Illinois more than 300 million years ago.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Getting kids where they need to go is a job in itself.
  • Uber is testing whether it can take on some of that driving.
  • The manufacturer's new pilot, Uber Kids, lets parents and guardians book rides for children ages 10 to 12 to take on their own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Getting kids where they need to go is a job in itself. Between school, extracurriculars, and appointments, families often piece together rides with help from relatives and other parents.

Uber is testing whether it can take on some of that driving.

The manufacturer's new pilot, Uber Kids, lets parents and guardians book rides for children ages 10 to 12 to take on their own. The service is available to select families in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin, starting Nov. 19. This comes after some rumors: Bloomberg first reported in August that Uber was developing the option.

Here's what parents should know before booking, from how to set up a ride to how to follow it in real time.

In a recent development, to book a ride, a parent or guardian first adds their child to the Family hub in the Uber app. Then they select the child as the rider. If the pilot is available to their family, Uber Kids will appear as a ride option, and the app will guide them through adding pickup and drop-off details.

Industry observers note that kids don't need their own Uber account or app. They can get updates about the trip by text at the number listed on their profile. Parents can request rides from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily, as long as a driver is available.

Each ride goes straight to one destination. A parent or the adult handling pickup can ride along, and kids ages 10 to 17 can join with their guardian’s permission, as long as the child the ride was booked for is in the car. And, if no Uber Kids driver is available, a child ages 10 to 12 needs an adult to ride with them in a regular Uber.

According to recent reports, A parent or another adult selected in the app must be at pickup to give the driver the PIN that starts the ride. If someone else needs to handle pickup or drop-off after booking, the guardian contacts the driver and sends the fresh adult the trip details and tracking link. Only the guardian can change the destination in the app.

Industry observers note that once the car is moving, the guardian can track it on a map, contact the driver, or tap "Watch" to see live video from the driver's phone. The driver gets a notification when the feed starts, and only the guardian and safety agents can watch it. Uber can flag an unexpected stop or route change so a safety agent can check in. Kids can also call their guardian or the support number in their trip texts. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sources indicate that at drop-off, the driver confirms the child reached the entrance or met the adult assigned to greet them. If that person hasn't arrived, the driver tries to reach them or the guardian, then calls Uber's safety line if nobody answers.

The app also makes a separate audio and video recording. Neither the guardian nor the driver can access it. Uber claims it receives the encrypted recording only if someone reports a safety incident. Otherwise, it’s deleted after 14 days.

According to recent reports, uber claims it invites experienced, highly rated drivers who have passed a background check. Drivers have to complete a training module on how Uber Kids trips work and turn on audio and video recording in the Driver app. Uber's driver guide explains how drivers should handle pickup and drop-off.

It's interesting that Uber is expanding to younger riders as it faces thousands of lawsuits from passengers who say they were sexually assaulted by drivers.

In a recent development, as of Nov. 2, 4,548 cases were pending in the coordinated federal litigation, according to the U.S. Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation. In February, a federal jury in Arizona found Uber liable and awarded $8.5 million to a woman who said a driver raped her when she was 19. And in April, a North Carolina jury awarded $5,000 in a related case after finding that a driver committed battery. (Uber settled another federal case in October before it went to trial.).

Uber has been giving teens a way to get around on their own since 2023. Kids ages 13 to 17 can request rides through an account linked to a parent's account, and Lyft offers a similar service in select areas called "Lyft Teen." When a child in the Uber Kids pilot turns 13, they can set up a teen account and request their own ride (or their parents can still do it for them).

In a recent development, families with younger kids already have options like HopSkipDrive, which takes riders as young as 6. The tech giant claims its drivers need at least five years of caregiving experience and must pass a fingerprint-based background check. There's no saying whether Uber utilizes similar investigations.

For plenty of families, getting to practice or a lesson still means a parent does the driving. In a 2025 survey by AP-NORC and HopSkipDrive, 75 percent of parents whose kids participated in extracurriculars noted they drove their kids themselves. When asked about the school commute, 28 percent of K–12 parents said they considered a hired ride, like a taxi, Uber, or Lyft, at least somewhat safe for their child.

This pilot will ultimately test whether features like a PIN at pickup and live video during the ride make parents comfortable enough to book one.

Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 ⁠on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state’s health department noted.

In a recent development, the department said the child was ⁠age four or younger. It did not disclose additional details, including the child’s vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy.

The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years.

Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,631 measles cases as of Friday.

Wisconsin has ⁠also reported two deaths, while Upcoming York state recorded its first measles-associated ​death, involving a ​child.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed six ​measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not ​specify the states ‌where the deaths were ​recorded.

A discrepancy between ​state and federal death tallies arose after the CDC, under the Trump administration’s health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.

Virginia has reported 220 measles ⁠cases so far in 2026, including 40 among children four years old or younger and 75 among those age five to 12, state ⁠health department data showed as of Thursday.

Of those cases, 179 involved unvaccinated individuals, 39 were associated with people ‌whose vaccination status was ‌unknown and two occurred with vaccinated individuals.

“Virginia has not had a measles-related death ‌since 1978,” said Frederic Bertley, immunologist and chief executive officer of the Center of Science and Industry. Bertley added that the measles virus infection is both alarming and evidence that measles is gaining a foothold and becoming a growing problem for the US.

It has been revealed that virginia health officials have reported increased measles activity driven largely by outbreaks ‌in the state’s central region. Buckingham county has reported 127 cases, the most in the state, while neighboring Charlotte county has recorded 34 ​cases.

BepiColombo finally reaches Mercury after eight-year odyssey

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
